Subject: Re: sudden p95 spikes and 503s on private cluster (urgent)

Marcus —

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95 latency and 5xxs across our private VPC deployment this afternoon (around 17:45 PDT). Node-level CPU is pegged on three nodes, throughput dropped ~35%, and several customer-facing endpoints returned 503. We attached the sampling logs and a topology snapshot.

We are on Redwood Private (v2.3.1), pinned model: open-tex-1.4q, serving config: 8xA10G (reserved), batch_size cap historically 64. No planned changes on our side before this window.

We urgently need:
- A quick RCA of what could cause simultaneous KV cache churn + CPU elevation
- A short-term mitigation that does not require full cluster redeploy (no long reboots)
- An ETA for a fix; CTO Mark Ruiz has asked for an exec sync if this will exceed 2 hours.

Attachments: sunnova-logs-20270913.tar.gz, sunnova-topology-snaps.zip

Thanks,
Aisha
Senior Ops Engineer
Sunnova Energy

Thanks for the heads up, Aisha — we see the error-rate uptick in our observability for your tenant as well. I'm looping in Irene (runtime team) and Laura (eng ops) to lead the triage.

Immediate triage plan (30-min window):
- We will collect kernel+nvml metrics and prefix/KV cache hit rates.
- Confirm whether a model variant rollout or quantization change landed in your cluster in the last 24h.
- If KV-cache eviction is driving extra work, we can temporarily raise the per-shard cache limit and tighten batch_window_ms to reduce burst compaction.
- If you can allow it, we recommend routing a small % (5%) of traffic to a hosted fallback while we stabilize. If not possible (data residency), we'll proceed with in-place tuning.

Can you confirm: current QPS sustained (avg and peak), and whether any scheduled jobs (nightly batch) overlapped the spike window?

Irene/Laura — can you take point for runbook actions? I'll prepare an exec note if ETA crosses 2h.

— Marcus

Redwood Inference

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@sunnova.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 19:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p95 spikes and 503s on private cluster (urgent)

Quick findings after the first pass on the logs Aisha sent:
- Correlated timeline shows high KV cache eviction rate starting 17:41 PDT; eviction counts spike right before CPU climbs.
- There was a rollout of an optimized quantized artifact (open-tex-1.4q-v2) 23 hours ago (per deployment metadata) — resource footprint for v2 increased peak working set by ~18%.
- Batch scheduling shows occasional micro-bursts where batch_window_ms was 8ms and batch_size cap 128. Those micro-bursts amplify memory pressure and cause compaction on the LRU cache.

Short-term mitigation plan (non-disruptive):
1) Patch runtime config to lower batch_size cap to 48 and reduce batch_window_ms to 4ms. This minimizes mem spikes and smooths CPU.
2) Increase KV cache per-shard quota by 20% to prevent immediate eviction storms.
3) Pin model variant back to open-tex-1.4q-v1 for the hot path (if you allow), or route 10% to v1.

I will push a small config patch that updates the per-tenant runtime knobs — this can be applied without a full restart; it triggers a rolling config reload per node (~30s per node to apply). Attaching the patch diff for your ops team to review: batch-config.patch

If Aisha confirms no hosted fallback allowed, we proceed with steps 1+2 now and schedule pin as step 3 (requires a brief canary eval).

Irene
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@sunnova.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 07:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden p95 spikes and 503s on private cluster (urgent)

Appreciate the quick analysis. Hosted fallback is not allowed due to data residency and our compliance rules.

Two questions:
- Will the config patch require a full service restart or rolling restart that causes client reconnects? We have a narrow maintenance window this afternoon (10:00–12:00 PDT) that execs prefer.
- If we pin back to v1, will that require re-quantizing or artifact re-pull that could be slower than the config change?

CTO Mark Ruiz is asking for an estimated timeline. If we can avoid service-level restarts and apply the patch with rolling reloads, we can approve an immediate apply outside the maintenance window. Otherwise we will schedule for the window.

Aisha

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: sudden p95 spikes and 503s on private cluster (urgent) — action plan and exec note

Executive summary and next steps:

What happened: a recent quantized variant increased hot working set and coupled with an aggressive batch cap produced KV cache eviction storms and CPU hotspots. That triggered higher tail latency and 503s.

Immediate remediation (apply now — no full restart):
- Apply batch-config.patch (Irene) — rolling config reloads, ~30s/node to apply.
- Increase KV cache per-shard quota by +20% (Laura) — dynamic change, no restart.
- Monitor p95 and 5xx for 45 minutes post-apply; if improvement < 30% then pin traffic to v1 for the hot path (requires artifact switch, ~8–12min to canary and validate).

Owners & timeline:
- Irene Choi: push config patch now and coordinate rolling reloads (ETA to apply across cluster: 6–9 minutes).
- Laura Bennett: update cache quotas and monitor infra side (parallel).
- Marcus Lin: send exec note and coordinate with Sunnova's ops for maintenance window if needed.

Related artifacts/tickets: SUP-11234 (priority), batch-config.patch (attached), sunnova-logs-20270913.tar.gz (for postmortem).

Request for Sunnova: please confirm you authorize us to apply the non-disruptive config changes immediately. If you prefer the scheduled maintenance window (10:00–12:00 PDT), let us know and we'll plan for a canary first.

Meeting: I scheduled a 20-min exec sync at 10:15 PDT in case you prefer the window (link above).

— Marcus Lin
